claims.text: The proposed model explicitly computes phonon dispersion and scattering in HfNbTaTiZr.
Mass and force-constant variations and 1 wt.% oxygen impurity scattering can be incorporated perturbatively into the model.
The proposed model will decouple lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions in HfNbTaTiZr.
The model's total thermal-conductivity estimates will be 20–30% more accurate than earlier Debye-temperature-based or defect-free estimates.
The low-temperature target material is equiatomic, defect-free HfNbTaTiZr below 200 K.
The high-temperature target material is HfNbTaTiZr containing a controlled 1 wt.% oxygen impurity between 300 and 1200 K.
Below 200 K, the lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions in HfNbTaTiZr are comparable.
For HfNbTaTiZr containing 1 wt.% oxygen, measured total thermal conductivity between 300 and 1200 K is 10–17 W/(K·m).
Mass and force-constant disorder and oxygen impurities modulate phonon scattering rates and lifetimes.
Changes in phonon scattering rates and lifetimes mediate the relationship between microscopic structure and macroscopic thermal transport.
Explicit phonon dispersions and lifetimes permit independent calculation of lattice thermal conductivity.
Combining independently calculated lattice conductivity with a separate electronic-conductivity estimate yields an improved total-conductivity prediction.
The predicted total thermal conductivity will match experiment within a 20–30% margin of error.
Below 200 K, the separately calculated lattice and electronic contributions will have comparable magnitudes.
Between 300 and 1200 K, the predicted total conductivity of the 1 wt.% oxygen specimen will fall within 10–17 W/(K·m).
Previous Debye-temperature-based or defect-free methods conflate lattice and electronic contributions.
The approach is applicable to equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr from the idealized oxygen-free state through samples containing up to 1 wt.% oxygen.
Reliability for non-equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr or oxygen concentrations above 1 wt.% is untested.
Phonon-electron coupling and additional scattering processes in real specimens may alter the claimed improvement.
A deviation greater than 30% between predicted and measured conductivity or its separated components is designated as falsifying the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis quantifies a 20–30% improvement relative to earlier methods, whereas the predicted outcome quantifies a 20–30% absolute error relative to experiment. Relative improvement and absolute prediction error are different metrics, so the stated numerical performance target is internally ambiguous.
